The glorious one, possessing a radiance equal to ten million moons, was constantly fanned on all sides by Rudra-maidens with yak-tail whisks and fans.
His self is fully satiated with the nectar of knowledge; he bestows the sovereign power of yoga;
and he possesses a serene face and eyes, constantly meditated upon by yogis. (10.637)
Shining as if laughing with its pure rays of moonlight, it destroys the darkness of ignorance and reveals the supreme form. (10.638)
To Rudra, the bestower of all happiness, who is surrounded by the host of Mothers,
the Goddess is seated upon his lap, possessing the luster of molten gold.
Worshipped by hosts of yoginīs, by practitioners, by gods, and by kinnaras,
she is complete with all auspicious marks and adorned with every ornament.
Bestowing the perfection of yoga and granting both liberation and worldly prosperity, Umā and Lalitā remain eternally facing the God, O Kṣaṇā. (10.641)
Śakti exists in the form of the other, and the possessor of Śakti is likewise Hara;
by the will of Śiva, he performs the creation and dissolution of the cosmic egg.
Those who, though devoid of initiation and specialized knowledge, are devoted to the worship of the Liṅga,
go to the abode of Hara, which brings the bliss of all sovereign powers.
Freed from old age and death, and devoid of disease and sorrow,
O Goddess, they do not go downward again into the ocean of suffering that is saṃsāra.
Then, beheld by Śrīkaṇṭha, they go upward to Śiva;
now learn from me that which is known as the world of Rudra, situated above this. (10.645)
But for the sake of progressive increase, they are situated as superior worlds:
below the Egg of Brahmā and above the realm of Rudra.
The city of Daṇḍapāṇi is to be known as being surrounded by various Rudras;
and the Lord Daṇḍapāṇi is endowed with the power of yogic sovereignty.
If it shines forth by its own will, even when restrained by the power of Daṇḍapāṇi, it reveals the path to liberation, which is otherwise so difficult to penetrate within the cosmic egg. || 10-648 ||
He was indeed worshipped according to the prescribed rite and meditated upon by the will of Śiva;
and I shall now describe, in brief, those Rudras who reside in the seven worlds.
Every Rudra, as well as Bhīma, Bhava, and likewise Agra, and Mahādeva and Īśāna— these are the lords of the world of Rudra.
Likewise, Brahmā resides in the world of Brahmā, Viṣṇu indeed in the city of Viṣṇu, and Rudra is established in the world of Rudra; they are remembered as the leaders of all.
O Varārohā, from Kālāgni to Daṇḍa, the distance of ninety-eight crores of yojanas has thus been described.
Furthermore, O fair-faced one, above that is the Kaṭāha, situated at a distance of ten million yojanas from the Brahmāṇḍa in the shape of a jar.
O fair-faced one, fifty koṭis above the surface of the earth, and fifty [yojanas] below it on all sides. (10.654)
Thus, O Goddess, a hundred crores [of such units] is called the earthly reality (pārthiva-tattva).
It should be known as extending up to the hundred Rudras, circular, golden, and even. (10.655)

O fair-faced one, that which is more solid than even the essence of a diamond and is impenetrable even by the gods, one should pierce it by means of the application of the *huṃ* and *phaṭ* syllables at the end. (10.656)
O Kṛśodarī, I shall now describe the Śatarudras in brief:
ten by ten, in due order, throughout the ten directions on all sides. (10.657)
I shall describe them in successive order according to the sequence beginning with the east:
Kapālīśa, Aja, Buddha, Vajradeha, and Pramardana. (10.658)
Vibhūti, Avyaya, Śāstṛ, Pinākin, and Tridaśādhipa—endowed with sovereign power, they overcame the strength of Indra. || 10-659 ||
The great gods, well-honored Indras and kings, investigate:
Agni, Rudra, Hutāśin, Piṅgala, Khādaka, and Hara. (10.670)
Jvalana, Dahana, Vabhru, Bhasmāntaka, Kṣayāntaka—
having overcome the power of Agni, they are endowed with sovereign might.
The great gods wander about, well-honored by King Agni:
Yama, Mṛtyuhara, Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Karta, and Kālina. || 10-672 ||
They are the uniter and the disuniter, as well as the establisher of dharma and adharma;
having overcome the power of Yama, they are endowed with sovereign might.
The great gods roam about, well-honored by King Yama;
Nairṛta, the slayer and destroyer, with his cruel gaze and terrifying form. (10.674)
Ūrdhvasepha, Virūpākṣa, Dhūmra, and Lohitadaṃṣṭravān, endowed with sovereign power, having overcome the strength of Nairṛti. (10.675)
The great gods, well-honored by the Nairṛtas, roam about;
namely Bala, Atibala, and the mighty Pāśahasta.
Śveta, Jayabhadra, Dīrghabāhu, Jalāntaga, Meghanādī, and Sunādī are thus briefly proclaimed. || 10-677 ||
Having overcome the power of Varuṇa,
those great gods, endowed with sovereign power and well-honored by Varuṇa, move about freely.
Swift, light, with the speed of wind, subtle, sharp, the ender of decay;
the ender of the five, five-crested, with matted hair, having clouds as his vehicle.
Having overcome the power of Vāyu,
those great gods, endowed with sovereign might and highly honored by Vāyurāja, move about freely.
The lord of treasures, handsome, fortunate, with a gentle body and wearing matted locks;
the bearer of Lakṣmī and jewels, the lover, the gracious one, and the illuminator. || 10-681 ||
Having overcome the power of Soma,
those great gods, endowed with sovereign might and highly honored by King Soma, roam about.
The Lord of Knowledge, the Omniscient, the Enjoyer of Wisdom, the Master of the Vedas;
the Lord of the Gods, the Eldest of All, the Protector of Beings, and the Beloved of Bali.
Authorized by Īśāna, O God, and endowed with the power of Īśa, the great gods wander about, presided over by the power of Īśa. || 10-684 ||
Vṛṣa, Vṛṣadhara, Ananta, Krodhin, Mārutāsana, Grasana, Durvasera, Phaṇīndra, and Vajradaṃṣṭravat. (10.685)
Having overcome the power of Viṣṇu,
those great gods, endowed with sovereign might and well-honored by Ananta, roam about.
Śambhu, Vibhu, Gaṇādhyakṣa, Rūpākṣa, and Tridaśeśvara;
Saṃvāha, Vivāha, Nabholipsu, and Trilocana. [10.687]
Having transcended the state of Brahmā, those great gods, endowed with sovereign power and well-honored by Brahmā himself, move about freely.
A retinue of one thousand is prescribed for each one;
known as the Śatarudras, they remain pervading the entire universe.
Innumerable thousands of gods who dwell in the directions below and above, moving everywhere at will, [remain so] even through kalpas and manvantaras.
And I shall describe each individual overlord, O fair-faced one:
situated indeed to the east of the egg is the one known by the name Śveta.
He was joined by ten Rudras of great heroism and prowess,
and with intensely blazing splendors like the rays of the sun.
In the southeast as well, there is the renowned one named Vaidyuta;
he too should be known as being surrounded on all sides by hundreds of Rudras.
In the southern region, O Goddess, Mahākāla stands, possessing the brilliance of the fire at the end of an eon,
surrounded by the hundred Rudras of immeasurable prowess.
In the southwest, the one named Vikaṭa stands surrounded by a hundred [attendants], possessing great splendor like a second sun. || 10.695 ||
In the western region, there is Rudra, renowned as Mahāvīrya;
he too remains surrounded by hundreds of Rudras of measured prowess.
And in the northwestern direction, the glorious and mighty Vāyuvega stands at the corner of the quarter, surrounded by a hundred [attendants]. || 10-697 ||
Surrounded by a hundred named Subhadrās from the north,
the heroic one, endowed with the power of great yoga, dwells there.
The Name-Rudra consisting of knowledge is established in the northeast;
surrounded by the hundred Rudras, Vāhurāṭ is situated above.
Endowed with the power of great yoga, he remains there with his heroic strides;
then another, Kālāgnirudra, stands there as the second.
Surrounded by hundreds of Rudras, O lady of beautiful countenance, he stood there;
surrounded by that hundred of Rudras, he was like the sun with its rays.
Above, Vīrabhadra is surrounded by the eleven great-souled Rudras of massive form, who have arisen from the wrath of Rudra.
And in this very manner, O Goddess of noble vows, each one of these ten great-souled ones is surrounded by a hundred Śatarudras.
The retinues of these great-souled ones are also incalculable;
they stand surrounding the cosmic egg like bees surrounding honey.
Just as a kadamba flower is surrounded by its filaments,
so indeed is the cosmic egg surrounded by Rudras of immeasurable prowess.
It was adorned on all sides with archways, doors, and panels variegated with various jewels, and with wonderful structures made of Jāmbūnada gold.
It was crowded with divine women and endowed with all objects of desire;
it was proclaimed as the Egg of Brahmā, a powerful web of nooses.
It is submerged in the great ocean of birth, disease, old age, and death;
it is shrouded by the impurities of the three qualities (guṇas) and agitated by manifold thoughts. || 10-708 ||
Deluded by the knowledge of sacrificial animals and agitated by the three states of existence, all disputants indeed remain within these very states of existence. (10.709)
Deluded, they do not understand the distinction between the higher and the lower;
for in the beginning, the golden egg was created, which is the very form of the world and is by nature subject to destruction.
This staff, which is possessed by the Māyā of the Lord for the welfare of his own class of beings,
has been fully described in brief, but not in detail.
Accompanied by a multitude of celestial palaces (vimānas) and resulting in various enjoyments as their fruit,
above that are the principles (tattvas), beginning with Āpa and ending with Śiva.

Arranged in ten ways through a progressive sequence of higher and higher stages, the principles (tattvas) extend from [the gross elements] up to primordial nature (prakṛti); and beyond that, they are further divided into a hundredfold.
One should know that [the stages] ending with Māyā extend upwards for a thousandfold;
above that, the level known as Īśvara is to be known for a hundred-thousandfold.
[Sādākhya], reaching to the limit of the peak (koṭiparyanta), extends upward to the end of the bindu and nāda;
indeed, that multitude of leagues remains pervading the Śakti.
Pervasive, it stands having pervaded all paths;
beyond that is the immeasurable, subtle, omnipresent Śiva. (10.716)
I shall fully declare the worlds in their proper sequence, beginning with their state of occurrence,
as well as the form of each world and the extent of the worlds.

That which is not seen by those with the knowledge of cattle, whose views are deluded by wrong paths, and which is indeed not seen even by those who have gone directly [to the truth], namely the followers of the Pañcarātra; || 10-718 ||

Neither by those who contemplate intrinsic nature, nor by those who advocate for karma, nor by those who maintain skeptical views, nor by those utterly deluded by the doctrine of "perhaps" (syādvāda), [is this state attained]. (10.719)
It cannot be known even by those who speak the truth, nor by worldly people;
neither by those who contemplate the self, nor by those who proclaim logical reasoning.
Nor by the Vaiśeṣikas who are devoted to the six categories, nor even by the proponents of Nyāya who argue from reasons and examples. (10.721)
Neither by those who maintain the doctrine of a single birth, nor by those who maintain the doctrine of multiple births,
nor by those in the world who maintain the doctrine of material form, is the Lord’s sovereignty ever fully understood.
There are three hundred such and other disputants as well, along with sixty-three others who are of deluded mind. (10.723)
It is the supreme opener for those blinded by the darkness of ignorance, and like an excellent boat, it is the ultimate means of crossing over for those mired in the mud of saṃsāra. (10.724)
This supreme dispeller of darkness for those blinded by great gloom has been received from the mouth of the Supreme Lord; it is the wonderful [teaching] obtained from the Parā [Vidyā]. (10.725)
O Goddess, listen with a one-pointed mind to this divine nectar of knowledge, which encompasses the vast extent of various worlds and possesses wonderful, marvelous forms. (10.726)
The infinite collection of worlds exists without interruption, like a honeycomb, and likewise has the form of a mass of earth. (10.727)
It has the form of a fish, a conch, or a lotus stalk; it is situated like a pomegranate seed;
it has the appearance of a *kadamba* filament; and its filling is like a heap of grain.
O fair-faced one, the infinite worlds are like the dwelling place of a great army, or like a dense cluster of trees in a forest, without any gaps between them. 10.729
There are various forms and variegated designs, made of all kinds of jewels;
they are circular, elongated, and shaped like half-moons.
Others have the form of smoke, others are shaped like *nandāvarta* [swastikas]; others have the form of lotuses, and others have the form of autumn clouds.
Forms shaped like mountains and those shaped like herds of elephants, others shaped like veins, and forms shaped like flames. || 10.732 ||
The forms of the great celestial palaces are like pikes,
others are shaped like drums, and there are cities shaped like triangles.
O fair-faced one, there are forms of the Great Being endowed with a hundred peaks,
as well as others with a thousand peaks and whirlpools.
There are other peaks numbering ten million and innumerable summits;
some are circular, some are square, and others are triangular.
There were divine variegated banners and divine bells and standards;
there were the sounds of the resonance of kettledrums and the like, as well as divine songs and standards.
The sounds of divine drums, the resonances of great lutes, and the noises of various musical instruments [fill] all the worlds at all times. (10.737)
They are as bright as mother-of-pearl, resembling crystal, and like parasols of ruby;
they have the color of moonstones and resemble strings of pearls.
O lady of excellent complexion, some are the color of lac juice, some have the hue of the indragopaka insect, and others are made of sapphire. (10.739)
Some have the color of the morning sun, others resemble the interior of a lotus; some possess the luster of the moon, and others resemble ten million moons.
At midday, they possess a uniform color resembling ten million suns;
they have the luster of *aśoka* flower clusters and resemble yellow orpiment.
They are the color of blue lotuses, resembling masses of lightning,
having the hue of Indra’s bow, and as white as cow’s milk.
The Sindūraka planets shine like Gorocanā, like molten gold, and like smokeless fire. (10.743)
Some worlds are the color of a white conch shell,
while others are of various colors and possess diverse forms and shapes.
Thus, O Goddess, beyond these is the supreme, all-pervading state, immeasurable, incalculable, and inaccessible to all disputants. (10.745)
Without the grace of the Lord, this knowledge is not obtained;
nor does meditative cultivation arise for an embodied being without having received initiation.
But when, due to a cause, the power that brings about liberation arises, then by the will of Śiva, that auspicious initiation consisting of consciousness descends upon him. (10.747)
Then, through the divine nature of mantra-yoga, the bound soul (paśu) attains liberation;
otherwise, they do not attain liberation even by means of hundreds of other types of knowledge.
He by whom all has been revealed by Śiva, who possesses infinite forms—he alone attains liberation; he is Śiva, Śarva, and Maheśvara.
Therefore, this primary knowledge was previously taught by me to you;
it is like a supreme boat for those submerged in the mire of saṃsāra.
Mahāmāyā perceives the Supreme Lord, who is beyond the sphere of ignorance, who transcends the realm of the bound, who is the infinite, the supreme, the agitated, and the easily understood. 10-751.
O beloved, listen with a one-pointed mind as I declare this divine nectar of knowledge, a wonder which I have obtained from the mouth of the Supreme Lord. 10.752
Above the egg of Brahmā, eleven worlds are recorded,
belonging to the eleven Rudras, whose splendor is equal to the fire at the end of an eon.
But above this, O fair-faced one, I shall describe the supreme [abode] of the Goddess:
divine, made of sapphire, and perfectly circular on all sides. (10.754)
In that place resides the Blessed Goddess Bhadrakālī,
dark as a blue lotus, with a complexion as radiant as smooth saffron.
Adorned with two mandalas having the form of solar discs, she shines like the twilight on the full moon night, illuminated by two moons. || 10.756 ||
And likewise, the necklace resting between her two breasts shines like a flowing stream between two dark collyrium-like eyes. (10.757)
And upon a divine throne supported by four lions of delightful prowess,
consisting entirely of vajra and adorned with divine jewels.
On a seat of radiant light, the goddesses possess a luster like that of pure collyrium;
they are situated upon the white peaks of the Himalayas and amidst dark blue clouds.
The divine Lake Mānasa, composed of all kinds of jewels, shines resplendently like an auspicious night adorned with yellow garlands at the rising of the moon in the western quarter.
His third eye, situated upon his forehead,
shines resplendent like the rising sun adorned with the flames of its rays.
She shone with a white umbrella held aloft, like the night graced by the moon situated above a dark cloud. || 10.762 ||
Surrounded by thousands of millions upon millions of women,
they were like the crescent moon in the vault of the sky encircled by the stars.
The women there have the complexions of white and blue lotuses, or are dark like gold; some are as dark as priyaṅgu buds, while others are as fair as the moon, all in the full bloom of youth.
Possessing forms as white as lotuses, with full hips, waists, and breasts,
they were knowledgeable in the methods of both existence and non-existence, and skilled in song and dance.
There, the women delight while worshipping that goddess with the sounds of flutes, lutes, drums, and other instruments made of bell-metal.
Thus, O fair-faced one, there is a world named Vijaya,
which is known in the world as Durgā among those residing within the interior of the cosmic egg.
Those who were to be known through austerity after first approaching the Supreme Lord were brought down for the sake of slaying the great-souled Mahiṣa.
And by that single horn, the Blessed Lord Himavat, the mountain, was destroyed by the Blessed Lady, cast away like a withered leaf. (10.769)
That goddess dispelled that darkness, rising like the sun;
that goddess abides through the names and forms of all the gods.
The Mother of Yoga, Pratisvecchā, Kumārī, and Lokabhāvanī—she is recited elsewhere as being inconceivable and immeasurable. (10.771)
In every kalpa, again and again, the Goddess, together with Viṣṇu,
comes as his sister despite the change in name and form.
In every Manvantara and likewise in every Yuga,
she acts for the benefit of all like a mother, for the sake of protecting the worlds.
Its name is Bhuvana, known by the title Vijaya;
those who are devoted to it and have been initiated into its mandala go there.
O lady of beautiful countenance, this cannot be attained through austerity, nor by sacrifices accompanied by abundant sacrificial fees, nor even by various kinds of gifts.
By the mere negligence of the God of gods, whose crest is marked by the crescent moon,
one who has received initiation may indeed attain the mandala of universal emperors.
The seedless initiation (nirbījadīkṣā), O Goddess, indeed bestows liberation;
it is the supreme initiation for emancipation, duly performed according to the rules. (10.777)
O fair-faced one, to whatever extent initiation from the enclosure of the Lords of Knowledge (vidyeśa) is performed for men,
to that same extent they attain their destination within the worlds.
The abodes of the Lords of the World (Bhuvaneśas) are established in their proper sequence;
I shall tell you all of this, so listen with one-pointed mind, O beloved. (10.779)
Beyond Bhadrakālī is the supreme deity Rudra, born from the wrath [of Śiva]; in Vīreśa, he possesses the radiance of the fire at the end of an eon, numbering ten million.
He possesses the thundering roar of the mass of clouds at the end of an eon;
O Śatavāhu, he is of great splendor and adorned with divine ornaments.
Dark as an autumn blue lotus, with a luster like black collyrium;
resembling the neck of a peacock, it is slightly pale and reddish.
It has the luster of a dark cloud, the radiance of an *atasī* flower,
resembles sapphire in some parts, and in others has the appearance of a bumblebee.
Having a form resembling natural collyrium, he was joined by the eleven Rudras and accompanied by thousands of millions of high-souled Rudras.
The world of that god is renowned by the name Vijaya;
it is divine, resembling sapphire, and vast, composed entirely of vajra.
O woman of excellent complexion, he was surrounded by ten thousand crores of Rudras, along with other multitudes of beings within the worlds.
He was surrounded on all sides by divine Rudras of great heroism, who were dark like the petals of a blue lotus and resembled the necks of peacocks.
With hymns of praise, auspicious rites, songs, and the sounding of dances and musical instruments;
with the sacred syllable *praṇava*, flutes, lutes, kettledrums, cymbals, and *ṛigomukha* drums. || 10.788 ||
With cymbals and trumpets, with conchs, drums, and *pīlukas*, with mṛdaṅgas, mountain caves, cymbal-clappers, and murajas as well. (10.789)
With *mondaka*, *āhala*, *taṅga*, *timi*, *lādra*, *ghaṭa*, and other instruments;
with cymbals (*vallita*), cymbal-clashes (*tāla*), and loud-sounding *mukhamardala* drums. || 10.790 ||
With parched laughter, loud bursts of laughter, roars,
and leaps;
with spirits, throngs of spirits, Rudras, chatterings, and likewise recitations.
By those meditating, by those chanting, by those running, and likewise by those standing still; and by others emitting the cries of peacocks and cuckoos.
Surrounded by those great-souled ones who were manifesting through various transformations of speech,
he was like the sun encircled by its rays of great splendor.
With elephant faces, horse faces, lion faces, and parrot-like faces; with cow-ear faces, ox-faces, and others such as leopard and bear faces. (10.794)
The Lord was attended by those with the faces of tigers and monkeys;
Vīrabhadra, of great splendor, possessed a radiance equal to the fire at the end of an eon.
The great seat of that deity consists entirely of vajra;
it is one hundred thousand [yojanas] in extent, square, and possesses the radiance of fire. (10.796)
And it shines, surrounded by lions of terrible prowess;
there dwell those of meritorious deeds who remember Maheśvara.
Whether in water, on dry land, or in fire, or even by the severing of their heads,
those who attain the realization of the Lord have gone to the city of Vīrabhadra.
O Goddess of the gods, above this world there is a great covering consisting of water and density,
standing like a rainbow.
There, upon that seat, the great-souled ones are the size of the tip of a thumb;
there, indeed, it is said to extend for ten million yojanas in width and height.
O Dear One, the watery covering extends threefold in width across;
by that, which spreads like a great cloud, everything is enveloped.
It is known as the Egg of Rudra (Rudrāṇḍa), and elsewhere as the World of Rudra (Rudraloka);
it is called the Abode of Vīrabhadra and the Dwelling of Bhadrakālī.
It was beautified by thirteen other worlds and adorned without any gaps by various divine hosts of Rudras.
O beloved, this [world] of Vīrabhadra is indeed like the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa);
hereafter, I shall describe the great world-sphere of Dharitrī.
In that world, the eternal and blessed Goddess Dhātrī,
having attained incomparable sovereignty over gold, remains established there in worship.
He was surrounded by many who bore the marks of universal monarchs,
and encompassed by hosts of beings and his own sons who were devoted to him.
Accompanied by the sounds of divine songs and the resonance of hundreds of musical instruments,
he was surrounded by hosts of Rudras from infinite multitudes of worlds.
In the midst of this world, [he is] like the rising sun,
resembling a red lotus, divine, and possessing the luster of an *aśoka* blossom.
In the midst of it, amidst divine multi-storied palaces made of rubies,
is the Blessed Lady Dharitrī, the sustainer of the world.
They are constantly adorned with garlands hanging from red wreaths,
and their cheeks are embellished by the splendor of the orbs of the moon and sun.
Clad in yellow golden garments and adorned with great necklaces,
they are stationed upon the back of a tortoise extending for a thousand yojanas.
They have four faces and eight arms, adorned with divine ornaments;
they are endowed with beauty and youth, and are experts in dance and song.
Thirty million divine women born of the mind, adorned with celestial ornaments, wait upon him, surrounding him on all sides.
All of them were created by him, desiring his welfare;
they resembled molten gold and were adorned with divine ornaments.
With a raised parasol being held over his head,
that one of great splendor stands upon the eastern side of the great mountain Meru.
Being worshipped by that goddess, the Lord of Mountains remains there,
dark-complexioned like the petal of a blue lotus and resembling a dark rain cloud.
A great mountain named Nīla, clothed in yellow garments and possessed of great splendor,
surpassed all others in beauty like another enemy of Kaiṭabha.
The Lord of Mountains, being worshipped by divine Naga women, is situated to his north; he resembles the moon and is adorned with ornaments such as a crown.
The great mountain named Śveta has the form of a white parasol;
to its north are those who shine like the sun and are adorned with crowns as ornaments. (10.818)
Wearing yellow garments, glorious like another flower-arrowed god (Kāmadeva), I shall speak with my right hand as well; listen, O beloved, for your own welfare.
With a splendor like the moon, radiant in energy, adorned with divine ornaments,
wearing white garments, and full of majesty, he was like a second Grandfather (Brahmā).
Resembling molten gold, adorned with divine ornaments,
wearing yellow garments, glorious, and anointed with yellow garlands and unguents.
The lordly Hemakūṭa, possessed of great splendor like Śaṅkara himself by his radiance,
shone like the sun enveloped in twilight.
Resembling a pale white hue, as white as a conch shell or cow’s milk, wearing white garments, glorious, and adorned with divine earrings. || 10-823 ||
With a great parasol being held over his head, the king appeared like a second King of the Gods from the north. || 10.824 ||
In the west is Gandhamādana, resembling an *indragopaka* insect; the glorious mountain wears red garments and stands like the sun set down. (10.825)
Resembling pure crystal, wearing white garments and garlands,
adorned with a crown and earrings, glorious and bearing a wreath, he stood in the east.
Thus surrounded by these and other mountains,
ending with the Lokāloka range, as well as by the Kulaparvatas.
The goddess who bears a divine form is indeed the supreme body of the Lord;
by the mere scent of her concentration (dhāraṇā), the yogi abandons his vital breath.
The earth assumes as many supreme forms as there are;
beyond that, O Goddess, lies the great oceanic world.
It is divine, consisting entirely of vajra, endowed with hundreds of divine wonders, possessing a luster like a cloud or a blue lotus, and perfectly circular in every direction. || 10-830 ||
In the center of this world, however, is a mandala resembling the moon,
one hundred thousand yojanas in circumference all around.
In its center, however, was a person of golden complexion and great luster,
wearing a crown, earrings, and garlands, adorned with divine ornaments.
The Lord Āpa, however, [assumed] the supreme form of Vāruṇī;
then, having surrounded that high-souled deity from all sides, [they stood] together.
Endowed with beauty and youth, she constantly attends upon him;
the goddess wears white garments and is anointed with incomparable white perfumes. (10.834)
Her body is adorned with a white sacrificial thread (*yajñopavīta*), beautified by a white necklace, and a white parasol is held over her head. (10.835)
And to his north stands the Gaṅgā, possessing a supreme form—
the goddess clad in blue garments, anointed with blue perfumes and unguents.
A blue garland is upon his neck, and the Yamunā is to his right;
thus the great rivers, surrounding him of great splendor, [are situated].
O Goddess of gods, the eight oceans, together with their own rivers as excellent women,
always worship with devotion her supreme form as Vāruṇī.

Having performed concentration (dhāraṇā) upon that very Lord of Gods, who consists of the subtle elements alone, [one perceives] various lakes, sacred fords, and those deities who are His devotees. (10.839)
The supreme maternal portion, consisting of water and earth, is the highest body of Varuṇa.
Beyond this, O woman of excellent complexion, I shall describe the world.
O Goddess, the abode of Śrī, renowned as Padmagarbha,
is filled with dense clusters of hundreds of celestial chariots standing in close proximity.
It was adorned by the lords of the worlds and by the Rudras as well as the hosts of Rudras;
it was beautified by divine lakes and lotus-pools of Lake Mānasa.
With lotuses the size of chariot wheels, adorned with jewels and gold,
possessing stalks of lapis lazuli and fragrant with divine scents.
It was adorned with soft, radiant, and variegated blossoming *vajra-kesara* flowers that resembled the orb of the moon. || 10.844 ||
It was adorned everywhere with various gardens filled with diverse birds, and with trees that provided all objects of desire.
With various wonderful pleasure-mountains made of many kinds of jewels, and with celestial women endowed with beauty and youth; (10.846)
It was adorned by divine women who were skilled in the methods of both existence and non-existence,
and by various jewel-lotuses possessing a radiance equal to diverse splendors.
It was graced by lords of kings who uttered hymns of praise and auspicious benedictions,
and it was filled with celestial women singing and dancing.
In that delightful world, there was a divine mandala, filled with rays of light and possessing a splendor equal to the interior of a lotus, resembling the autumnal moon.
In its center is the Blessed Lady Śrī herself, the Illuminator of the World; she revolves a radiance of four thousand million [rays]. (10.850)
In one place, their splendors are perceived as if joined together like a pair;
they are as if extinguished, yet captivating with all-encompassing bliss. (10.851)
The supreme goddess is embodied and her form is unfailing;
she extends for a hundred yojanas, possessing a radiance like that of the rising sun.
Upon a lotus made of moonlight, with a vajra-stamen and pericarp, possessing ten million petals, most divine, and endowed with the qualities of fragrance and touch. (10.853)
Seated in the lotus posture, the Blessed Lady possesses a radiance equal to the interior of a lotus; she is eternally above, supreme through her supreme majesty.
And with great jewels, there is a beautiful, hanging garland of flowers; on the surface of the cheeks, there is a shimmering play of rays of light. (10.855)
Wearing earrings resembling the orb of the sun,
she bore a multitude of shimmering faces and possessed all aesthetic flavors.
Clad in golden and yellow garments, adorned with great necklaces, and with a moon-like parasol being held over their heads. || 10.857 ||
The Blessed One, the Supreme Goddess Sātantū, was surrounded by Gandharvas born of Rudra who were singing her praises.
She, who was attained by the powerful Viṣṇu after propitiating him with ascetic penance,
and who was given by Śvetapīta, now wears the garments of one afflicted by separation.
That Blessed Lady is established upon the body of Viṣṇu with one half;
with one quarter she is on the body of the god Indra, and with a quarter of a quarter she resides in heaven.
Furthermore, O Goddess, they are well-established in the earthly realm with half of that [measure];
and humans indeed abide with half of that, pervading [the world] with their forms.
She is proclaimed to be twofold: both with form and formless;
she remains there immovable, subtle in body, and unshakable. (10.862)
O observer of excellent vows, one who dies at Rudrakrīḍāvatāra, Prayāga, and other such sites, and especially at Śrīgiri, shall go to the world of Śiva.
This beloved one has been described as being for the enjoyment of others;
may such a goddess as this, along with sovereignty, the power of atomization (aṇimā), and the other [siddhis], be attained.
Having become eightfold and divine, she abides even among the gods;
that goddess is said to be the supreme accomplishment (siddhi) even for the Siddhas.
Today you have engaged in a terrible and incalculable battle with Tāraka and the other lords of the thirty gods, who were all desirous of attaining that same prosperity.
Innumerable battles have indeed been waged by the universal monarchs;
and the connection of those who are liberated with those who are unawakened is considered supreme. (10.867)
Henceforth I shall proclaim the world; listen attentively.
It is known as Sārasvata and is also remembered as Gāndharva. (10.868)
Or, O observer of excellent vows, within a city in the heart of a lotus,
it is declared to be ten million yojanas in extent on all sides.
It was divine, composed of all kinds of jewels, endowed with every sovereignty,
and filled with auspicious celestial palaces of various forms made of many gems.
There were Gandharvas and humans singing in many ways,
as well as others dancing, along with various groups attending at his side.
It was crowded with beautiful women and Gandharvas;
in its center, O Goddess of Gods, was a splendid [palace] resembling the autumn moon. (10.872)
A blazing, circular mandala, filled with a garland of rays, is perfectly round;
in its center is established the Blessed Lady Sarasvatī.
Possessing a splendor like that of a thousand autumn moons,
the goddess wears yellow garments and has eyes as broad as lotus petals.
Dark-complexioned like the petals of a blue lotus, adorned with divine ornaments,
draped in golden bands, and wearing celestial earrings.
And she bore upon her breast a great necklace with the luster of the moon,
adorned with a pair of earrings from which clusters of shimmering rays radiated.

The goddess Sandhyā has three villages as her folds; she is auspicious, with the seven musical notes as her body, breasts, hair, and downy growths, and she bears the Mūrchanās as the hairs upon her limbs.
O fair-faced one, the chandoha is the hands and creepers, the srotas is the radiance of the complexion, and the joints are the fingers; these indeed are the characteristics. 10.878.

Seated upon that supreme, divine throne, she who is the auspicious stability of the entire world appears like Stability itself, surrounded by the lords of the hosts of beings, both manifest and unmanifest.
With the Mānasābhiśvana women and likewise with the Mānasa Gandharvas—
Hāhā, Hūhū, Citraratha, Tumbaru, and Nārada as well.
Viśvāvasu, Viśvaratha, and those skilled in divine song—having mentally united with the Self and abandoned desire for the fruits of action. [56b] 10-881 ||
O Goddess worshipped by the gods, those who have reached the sacred site of Śārasvata, as well as others who maintain the dhāraṇī, are indeed liberated even at their death. (10.882)
Those best of men also attain the station of Sarasvatī;
for that Goddess Sarasvatī is indeed the very form of the Supreme Lord.
That Goddess, who exists by way of her transcendent aspect within the interior of the cosmic egg and in the world of Brahmā, stands upon a single foot.
Or else, it is half that of Śakra, and half of that for the Gandharvas;
half of that for the Siddhas, and half of that for the Kinnaras. || 10-885 ||
And above that, among the Nāgas, Yakṣas, and Arhats, it likewise remains; from the Piśācas, it exists in human beings as a thousandth part.
Having performed severe penance and having propitiated the wielder of the Pināka bow,
those goddesses, adorned by the Lord, were brought down in various forms.
In the past, at the beginning of the kalpa, as Brahmā was recollecting her,
she emerged from those very sounds being remembered, endowed with a beautiful form.
She emerged from the seven notes of Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest;
because she issued forth from those notes, she is therefore Sarasvatī.
She stands as the foundation of all scriptures and resides within the poetry of poets;
she is the enhancer of the intelligence and intellect of all the sages.
She indeed possesses all knowledge; she is omniscient and honored by the gods.
Her city is proclaimed to be on the northwestern side of Mount Meru.
This supreme world of Sarasvatī has been proclaimed by me to you; thus has the supreme body of the Goddess been glorified.
And here, indeed, listen to the most excellent of worlds, which are free from calamity: Amareśvara, Prabhāsa, Naimiṣa, and likewise Puṣkara.
Āṣāḍhin, Diṇḍimuṇḍin, and the impure Bhārabhūti are known as the "One in the Secret" among those who dwell in the enclosure of water.
I shall now describe, in brief, that which is situated above the realm of fire; listen to it, O fair-faced one, for it is a divine world. (10.895)
Bearing a brilliance emanating from all sides from its clusters of *aśoka* blossoms, it possesses the luster of a fully bloomed *kiṃśuka* flower and resembles the *javā* flower.
In the center of this world, there is said to be a circular mandala of fire, possessing a radiance equal to the risen sun.
In its center, however, is the Lord Śivāgni, the supreme cause;
having descended into the middle, he stands there in a threefold and again a threefold manner.
In the mouth of that Rudra, the Supreme Self, the Earth exists in the form of the tongue; thus is Nīlalohita. (10.899)
Moreover, that very god is himself the Lord Kālāgni;
I shall describe his form—listen attentively, O beloved.
Having the luster of the petals of a red lotus and a brilliance equal to a ruby,
O Śrī, he wears red garments and is adorned with red garlands and unguents.
With his auspicious face adorned by two earrings that possess the brilliance of the sun, he shines with a chest illuminated by a magnificent necklace.
Wearing a crown and earrings, radiant, he is called the god-faced one;
the Lord himself is seated above upon a pedestal composed entirely of vajras.
Like a divine fire arisen from the friction of bamboos on a mountain peak,
he [manifested] ten thousand times ten million lords of the fiery hosts.
Emerging from the southern mouth of this self-existent Svayambhū,
these Rudras, possessing the splendor of the sun, indeed exist for the welfare of all the worlds.
And there, noble women, skilled in various divine songs, constantly attend upon that great-souled fire.
The Gaṇas, Rudras, Bhūtas, and Kinkaras by the thousands—
all these have been consumed by the fire of Śiva during the supreme oblations to the Lord.
In the ritual procedures for fire-offerings, that which is constantly offered by those who know the method reaches Īśvara as that Fire; having known the object of knowledge, however, it is *dhāraṇā*.
He indeed exists pervading the worlds in one way and in many ways;
he is the radiant source of all radiance, therefore the sacrifice is the maker of day.
He who, having manifested himself in many ways throughout the various intermediate kalpas, appeared on the surface of the earth through fifty different births.
Having thus correctly described that great Āgneya world,
I shall hereafter describe the worlds and their presiding deities.
Hariścandra, Śrīśaila, Jalpa, Mañjātikeśvara,
Mahākālavana, and likewise the supreme Madhyama.
Kedāra and Bhairava have thus been briefly proclaimed;
they are declared to be extremely secret, starting from the east and proceeding in order up to the northeast.
Above this is the path of the covering; situated there, in the midst of the wind, is the world named Prāṇa, O lady of excellent complexion, belonging to Vāyu.
White as a conch shell or cow’s milk, with a radiance like that of snow, the kunda flower, or the moon;
and within it, [was a city] endowed with divine worlds and hundreds of divine wonders. (10.915)
In the center, however, was a divine maṇḍala with a radiance equal to a hundred moons, filled with rays of light, divine, and illuminating the ten directions. || 10-916 ||
In the midst of that, indeed, was the god Vāyu in his supreme form—
wearing a crown and earrings, radiant, and adorned with necklaces and armlets.
His limbs were variegated with various ornaments; he was adorned with wonderful garlands and unguents;
wearing splendid garments, the glorious one was decorated with great necklaces.
Indeed, ten crores of the high-souled gods named Mārutās worship that Great Soul,
the one of great splendor who has Vāyu as his form.
The all-pervading Lord, having pervaded bodies, manifests as one, as five, as seven, and indeed as sevenfold again; the omnipresent one possesses qualities such as horizontal movement and the rest.
Along with its mandala, one supreme body shines forth within the great divine [mandala];
yogins perceive that single self of the vital breath as tenfold.
Having meditated and abandoned the vital breaths, and having performed concentration (*dhāraṇā*) upon that,
those great-souled ones enter it, their forms becoming like the wind.
Thus, O lady of virtuous vows, the world named Prāṇa has been fully described to you;
therein dwell the Rudras as lords of that world, whom I shall now recount in due order.
Gaya, Kurukṣetra, Nakhala, and likewise Kanakhala;
Vimala, Aṭṭahāsa, Mahendra, and Bhīma—the eight [holy sites].
For this should be known as the most secret of secrets, preeminent above all:
in space, indeed, is space, pure and stainless like clear crystal. (10.925)
The yogi who is established in that state which is subtle in form, eternal, and situated in the middle region, and who is engaged in the concentration on space, is united with that supreme state.
In that space, I shall declare those Rudras who are established there,
abiding in the state of ten million Rudras, the Great Abode (Mahālaya) which is utterly liberated.
Gokarṇa, Bhadrakarṇa, Svarṇākṣa, and Sthāṇu as the eighth—
this indeed is proclaimed as the group of eight purifiers (pavitrāṣṭaka) in brief.
O Rudras, understand from me the unobstructed ego-sense therein:
Chagalāṇḍa, Durāḍa, Mākoṭa, and Maṇḍaleśvara. (10.929)
Kālañjara, Śaṅkukarṇa, Chagaleśvara, and Sthaleśvara—
these are declared to be the eight sacred sites (sthāna), which are beyond the range of the directions starting from the east up to the northeast.
Rudra, the Lord and Master of the Ego (ahaṃkāreśvara), resides in the Middle Country;
he is white, red, yellow, black, and has the luster of crystal.
The colors in the group of eight are briefly proclaimed as follows:
white, red, black, blue, dark green, pale yellow, and yellow. (10.932)
O fair-faced one, they are white, tawny, and smoky according to their various colors;
they are known as the hundred Rudras, three-eyed and holding tridents in their hands.
All the Rudras have the crescent moon as their crest-jewel and are accompanied by the Rudrāṇīs;
know that the world of the hundred Rudras is shaped like a lotus.
O Dear One, the fifty-eight worlds are said to be shaped like a tortoise,
situated within half of the space-covering [sphere] below the ego-principle (ahaṃkāra).
I shall now describe the other worlds; listen with a one-pointed mind.
First, however, is the great and vast mandala of the subtle element of smell (gandhatanmātra).
O Goddess, it stands like a celestial chariot (*vimāna*), extending for ten million *yojanas*.
O lady of excellent complexion, it is white, red, black, yellow, and green;
endowed with these five colors, its radiance is equal to that of Indra’s bow.
O Goddess of the gods, it is like a celestial chariot, perfectly circular in every respect.
If everything exists within the heart of the one who knows,
then from that [consciousness], impelled by the Lord of All, the earth is born.
Above that maṇḍala, O beloved, is the maṇḍala of the subtle element of taste (rasa-tanmātra),
dark like an emerald and resembling the feathers of a bow.
Existence (bhava) alone is established there as the Lord within the heart;
therefore, impelled by the Lord of the Earth, he emerged from the waters. || 10.941 ||
Above that mandala, however, is the form of the subtle element mandala, throbbing with a brilliance like the rays of the sun and possessing a luster equal to a ruby. || 10.942 ||
There, Rudra Paśupati alone presides;
from him, by the will of Paśupati, that splendor indeed issued forth.
O lady of excellent complexion, that fire pervades all the worlds;
above that mandala, however, is the mandala of the subtle element of touch (sparśa-tanmātra).
O beloved, the mandala of Vāyu has a luster like the dawn-red;
it is circular on all sides and resembles the shape of a canopy.
In that very mandala, O Goddess, Īśāna is firmly established;
from him, O Beloved, Vāyu has emerged, impelled by the will of Īśa.
Therefore, the arising of the vital breath consists of the five winds; it is the supreme pervader.
It proceeds in seven ways and seven ways, becoming manifold within a single month. || 10.947 ||
Above that mandala, however, is the mandala of the subtle element of sound (śabdatanmātra);
it is dark blue like the petal of a blue lotus, with a luster equal to still water. || 10.948 ||
Having a form like a canopy and perfectly circular on all sides, Bhīma is said to be its presiding lord; it stands at thirty-one [yojanas]. || 10-949 ||
Therefore, O beloved, that great [power] emerged from the sky, impelled by Bhīma’s will; it pervades all worlds and has attained the state of both the supreme and the non-supreme.
And above that mandala, the sun-mandala is described, resembling a thousand suns and blazing forth on all sides. || 10-951 ||
Blazing with the rays of celestial chariots and perfectly circular on all sides,
Rudra alone dwells there as the lord within the heart.
O fair-faced one, at the end of every eon, the suns depart from that [place];
and above that mandala is said to be the lunar mandala.
With a mandala equal in brilliance to thousands of millions of moons,
the Lord Mahādeva alone remains.
Therefore, the Rudras of the lunar digit, impelled by Mahādeva,
have emerged in countless thousands in every kalpa.
Above that maṇḍala, however, is said to be the Vedamaṇḍala;
it has a luster equal to ten million moons and is perfectly circular on all sides. (10.956)
It stands like consciousness, divine, presided over by Ugrasena;
it is fully expanded, moving to the left, and has indeed emerged from that very place.
Thousands of sacrificers have emerged in every kalpa through the fierce austerity of Brahmā, impelled by Ugrasena.
The Vedas and the various sacrifices, which exist within the infinite Brahman,
proceed from that [source] upward, as do the fruits of sacrifice.
Austerity and gifts, O Goddess of the gods, are governed by the Vāma-śakti;
thus these eight bodies of His are proclaimed as the supreme (parā).
Others are situated pervading the entire egg of Brahmā;
and beyond these is the mandala consisting of the instruments of action.
White, red, black, yellow, and green— by way of color,
these remain within the mandala which consists of the instruments.
In that [unmanifested state], activities proceed; therefore, for all differentiated beings, there are speech, hands, feet, the anus, and the generative organ as the fifth. (10.963)
From these [elements] arises that which is called the illuminator (prakāśaka), which resembles the stability of the supreme;
from that indeed proceed the five sense organs of cognition (buddhīndriya).
The tongue, the skin, the ear, the nose, and the eye are indeed in the body;
their objects, beginning with form, are situated within the sphere of fire (tejo-maṇḍala). || 10-965 ||
O lady of excellent complexion, these indeed have been proclaimed as the impellers (codaka);
and beyond these, there is that which resembles the four mandalas.
And from that vast, unchanging expanse, a circle of rays radiates in all directions;
from it indeed proceed the five objects for all embodied beings.
Sound, touch, beautiful form, taste, and smell as the fifth—
from these, moreover, beyond them, is the gentle orb of Soma.
Therefore, having emerged from the self by means of fifteen rays,
it is that which sets in motion the mind (citta), the intellect (cetas), and the thought-organ (manas), as well as sound and the other sense objects.
Therein resides the Lord of great splendor, Candramas, possessing gentle radiance.
Above that mandala, however, is a supreme and great mandala.
Resembling a hibiscus flower and like the rising sun,
it is, as before, equal in size and perfectly circular on all sides.
From that mandala, O Goddess, there arises ego (ahaṃkāra), possessing the great luster of the dawn-red twilight and resembling a smoky fire. (10.972)
Therefore, the internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa) resides within the self, by which this world is colored; like a blind man approaching a forest fire with a lamp held inside his garment. || 10.973 ||
Rudra is indeed his presiding deity; by him the noble one is always impelled.
O Goddess of the gods, this was previously told by me regarding Chagalaṇḍa.
But for one who knows that the principle of intellect (buddhitattva) lies outside the ego (ahaṃkāra),
it possesses a splendor equal to the radiance of thousands of millions of suns.
Listen now to the description of the world of the eight classes of divine beings;
there is a world named Kakubha, possessing a radiance equal to the dawn of twilight.
It was crowded with joyful women who delighted the mind,
while the Piśācas possessed enchanting splendor, with a radiance equal to the redness of twilight.
There, among those inhabitants numbering ten thousand crores,
there was a great and famous lord of the piśācas named Sunanda.
Possessing a luster like the dawn-red and the hue of the bandhūka flower,
he was adorned with earrings, and decorated with necklaces and armlets.
Wearing a crown, armlets, and a garland, clad in beautiful golden raiment,
he was surrounded by terrifying spirits stationed at his sides.
By those divine beings who assume various forms, adorned with celestial ornaments, possessing divine garlands and unguents, and endowed with divine sovereignty. || 10.981 ||
Surrounded by hosts of great splendor like a great multitude,
I shall hereafter describe the vast realm of the Rākṣasas.
In that divine world, endowed with hundreds of celestial sovereignties, [he saw] one resembling the throat of a cuckoo and like a dark blue cloud.
The great lord of the Rākṣasas named Karāla, resembling natural collyrium, wearing a crown and earrings, shone there with blazing and immense splendor. || 10.984 ||
Resplendent and made of precious collyrium, like a mountain of forest fire,
there were ten thousand koṭis of Rākṣasas named Muditā.
In this springtime, the great-souled one possesses a luster like that of a bumblebee or a rain-cloud.
Hereafter, I shall describe the great world of the Yakṣas.
Divine, made of Jāmbūnada gold, blazing with all kinds of jewels, perfectly filled with enjoyments and sovereign power, and circular in every direction. || 10-987 ||
In that world, however, there was a king of the yakṣas named Rudra;
he had the luster of molten gold and was adorned with ornaments such as a crown.
Surrounded by ten thousand times ten million gandharvas, who resemble realgar in appearance and are like yellow orpiment; 10.989b–g.
The Gandharvas named Sukāntas, adorned with variegated garlands and ointments, wearing wonderful garments, themselves marvelous, and decorated with diverse ornaments.
The head, known as Vṛhaṃbhoga, indeed grants all desires;
it is as white as a conch shell or cow’s milk, possessing a luster like that of a conch, a kunda flower, or the moon.
In that divine world, endowed with hundreds of celestial wonders,
there dwells the Lord named Vibhūti, the Indra and sovereign of that realm.
Resembling the orb of the moon, adorned with strings of pearls,
wearing white garments, glorious, and anointed with white garlands and unguents.
His crown was blazing, his splendor radiant, and he was adorned with two earrings;
he was further embellished by necklaces, armlets, bracelets, a white garment, and a white turban.
Indeed, there were two gods named Bhūtajā, endowed with supreme majesty;
they wore crowns and earrings, and were adorned with divine garlands.
Ten thousand times ten million gods, including Indras, are proclaimed;
surrounded by them, he of great splendor is like the moon among the stars.
The auspicious world named Mañja is like the autumn moon;
it is radiant like pure white clouds and possesses the brilliant luster of a pearl necklace.
There, the moon is indeed known as Amṛta, most excellent;
he resembles white crystal and always wears white garments.
Adorned with earrings of blazing splendor, he shines resplendent;
his limbs are anointed with divine perfumes and he is decorated with celestial ornaments.
There, those rays known by the name Raśmivyūhasamaprabha are to be understood as the gentle deities, arisen from the splendor of Soma.
There are indeed ten thousand crores of those worlds belonging to Soma’s splendor;
and above that, O Goddess of the gods, the world of Prajāpati is said to be located.
In that divine realm, he of immeasurable splendor was Prajāpati himself—
possessing universal form, universal color, and adorned with all ornaments.
The Universal Soul was surrounded by gods bearing universal forms;
there were ten thousand times ten million Viśvas of elemental splendor.
Surrounding the Great-Souled One, they wait upon him in splendor;
and his mind thereafter becomes like that of Brahmā, white as a conch shell or cow’s milk.
O God, the Grandfather (Brahmā) is indeed here, seated upon a white lotus, possessing a serene countenance;
he wears white garments, is glorious, and is anointed with white perfumes and unguents.
Wearing a white sacred thread and adorned with great necklaces,
he possesses a radiance equal to ten thousand times ten million lunar discs.
Surrounded by the Brahma-gods, he was indeed like the moon amidst autumnal clouds;
[he beheld] the Piśāca, Rākṣasa, Yakṣa, Gāndharva, and Aindra [realms].
The gentle Prajāpati Brahmā is remembered as the eighth among the divine classes;
for these indeed are the abodes and cities within the wombs of the gods.
For as he contemplates his descent into birth, these [manifestations] arise by the command of the Supreme Lord and impelled by Māyā.

Having entered the womb and the state of determination (niyāma), they manifest at the beginning of creation in manifold ways through various forms and abodes, belonging to Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest.
O lady of excellent hips, by means of a mere portion [of his power], he abandons his abode;
one should thoroughly purify the self together with the eightfold city and the senses.
Having thus purified with effort the five groups of eight, the eight forms, and the principle of intellect (buddhi-tattva) in due order, one should thereafter [purify] the eightfold group of Krodhas.
Samvarta, Tvakavīra, Kṛtānta, Jananāśaka, Mṛtyuhantā, Raktākṣa, Mahākrodha, and Sudurjaya. || 10-1013 ||
Their worlds indeed possess the luster of the petals of blue lotuses;
each one has a retinue of ten thousand crores.
Above the eight Lords of Wrath (Krodheśvaras) stands the great group of eight Splendors (Tejāṣṭaka):
Valādhyakṣa, Gaṇādhyakṣa, Sridaśa, and Tripurāntaka. || 10.1015 ||
Sarvarūpa, Śānta, and Nimeṣonmeṣa—these constitute the retinue consisting of fifteen thousand. || 10.1016 ||
For these are known as the Agnis and Rudras; by their splendor, they are black in color.
Their worlds, moreover, are variegated and shaped like tortoises.
Therefore, I shall describe the eightfold yoga in brief, but not in detail:
Akṛta, Kṛta, Bhairava, and Brahma. (10.1018)
The Vaiṣṇava, the Kaumāra, the Auma, and the Śrīkaṇṭha—
this is the station of the yogins, free from all dualities.
There the yogins sport with worlds possessing the luster of crystal;
there the Blessed Mother of the World herself is established.
Umā, the consort of Umā, the source of the universe, born of herself;
she who resembles molten gold and possesses a radiance equal to the rising sun. (10.1021)
Upon a magnificent, auspicious, jewel-encrusted great throne, surrounded by eight lions,
extending for a hundred yojanas and adorned with divine garlands.
The goddess Divyakuṇḍalinī, adorned with a great necklace,
is highly fortunate at the forefront of victory, possessing a form like that of Śrī herself.
And Jayā, who has the luster of the interior of a lotus and is adorned with all ornaments;
and Nandā, whose eyes are like lotus petals and who is adorned with necklaces and armlets. || 10.1024 ||
And Sunandā and Manoharā, their limbs adorned with all kinds of ornaments,
stood surrounding the female doorkeepers on every side.
Twenty thousand crores and twenty hundred crores of divine women from the Mānasa lake always attend upon him.
And there is one *vimāna* belonging to the Rudras of immense splendor, known as *Aumā*, which is endowed with every enjoyment. (10.1027)
They attend upon that goddess always as a son attends his mother;
descend into her midst along with me, O lady of beautiful countenance. (10.1028)
For the sake of favoring the worlds, she manifested in the eternal [tradition]:
as the Mother of the World (Jaganmātā) and the Source of the World (Jagadyoni) in the first kalpa; in the second, she was named Śāmbhavī; in the fourth, Viśvarūpiṇī;
in the fifth, O lady of beautiful hips, she was again considered Gaurī in the sixth.
The beautiful and auspicious daughter of Dakṣa was fair-complexioned; moreover, Svātañtu was the daughter of Dakṣa’s own sister.
The digit of the moon known as Amā, which occurs on the seventh day of the dark fortnight,
was again propitiated by Himavat and made his own daughter.
O beloved, having performed extremely difficult penance for half an eon, you have now become my wife; thus, O one whose body hairs stand on end with joy, you have been born again.
O fair-faced one, I am the dweller of Kailāsa together with you;
you are the body of my left side, and you are never separated from me.
Born again at Dakṣa’s sacrifice under the name Bhadrakālī,
she was indeed one and yet another form issued forth from the Lord.
Having reached this cycle of four yugas, during the Dvāpara age, she was born as Kṛṣṇapiṅgalā together with Viṣṇu for the purpose of slaying Mahiṣa.
Known by various synonymous names such as Kātyāyanī and Durgā,
she is the bestower of boons upon devoted human beings and is affectionate toward those who possess devotion.
Having already descended upon the summit of the Vindhya mountain,
O woman of excellent complexion, I shall hereafter describe the world.
Renowned as Sucāru, it resembles a thousand suns;
it has the form of a peak of Mount Kailāsa and the luster of white crystal.
Covered by millions of great canopies belonging to the universal monarchs,
in that divine world there was one whose splendor was equal to ten million suns.
He has a thousand arms and feet, and a thousand eyes;
he is the Lord of Umā, the Master of the World, the supreme bestower of grace upon all.
"This is indeed my place of enjoyment; situated there, born from the left side, it extends for a hundred thousand yojanas and is variegated with various jewels. (10.1042)
Upon a supreme, divine seat, covered with celestial coverings, radiant as a hundred suns, and variegated with jewel-lotuses.
Seated there, he of great splendor was surrounded by eight bull-demons;
he wore garments of golden silk and was adorned with necklaces and armlets.

Upon his great head, he wore a crown blazing like a mass of rain-clouds and resembling the orb of the sun; it was intensely radiant and fierce, like a peak of Mount Kailāsa, adorned with clusters of shimmering rays and earrings filled with light, and variegated with divine jewels.
And Pralamba, by the power of his great necklace, fell amidst a mass of rays like a waterfall cascading from a peak of the Himalayas onto the Ganges.
With thirty thousand crores and even three hundred crores [of beings],
armed with tridents, wearing matted hair, possessing three eyes, and adorned with divine ornaments. (10.1048)
He was surrounded by Rudras assuming various forms as well as hosts of spirits,
and encircled by celestial women born of his mind.
Indeed, he was surrounded by hundreds of millions of celestial palaces;
and all seven of the Rūpinī Mothers were adorned with various ornaments.
Surrounding that Great Being from all sides,
there stood the goddess Brahmī, with a complexion like the petals of a lotus and adorned with divine garments.
O Goddess of gods, she stands in the south-eastern direction like another Śrī;
O lady of beautiful countenance, she resembles a conch shell or cow’s milk in the north-eastern direction.
The goddess Māheśvarī, of great splendor and worshipped by the gods, stands there;
and Kaumārī, possessing the luster of the interior of a lotus and adorned with necklaces and armlets. || 10.1053 ||
In the northern direction, O Goddess of the Gods, Kāminī attends upon him;
she resembles a glossy blue lotus and is adorned with necklaces and earrings. (10.1054)
In the southern direction, O Goddess of gods, they worship that all-pervading one, who is renowned as Vaiṣṇavī by Śiva, the Supreme Self. (10.1055)
Resembling a dark blue cloud and adorned with all ornaments,
O Goddess of gods, Vārāhī attends upon you in the western quarter.
White as a swan, jasmine, or the moon, adorned with necklaces and earrings,
that goddess Aindrāṇī attends upon [the Lord] in the eastern direction.
Terror-inspiring, radiant, and adorned with all ornaments,
Cāmuṇḍā worships the Supreme Lord in the south-western direction.
Endowed with all their essential natures, they do not abandon that god;
yet, by means of a portion of themselves, they have been brought down to the world of men by Brahmā and the others.
For the sake of slaying the Asuras and for the welfare of human beings,
a most formidable penance was performed by Brahmā, the creator of the worlds.
And for the very purpose of slaying Ruru, they were brought down by me;
others, independent and supreme, remain stationed in the highest heaven.
They attend upon him at will, according to the distinction between higher and lower;
Umā indeed becomes sevenfold through the transformations of name and form.
Thus that Blessed Lord, surrounded by his mothers,
remained there, radiant with supreme splendor, illuminating the world.
Above him likewise are the eight forms of that wise one:
Śarva, Bhava, the Lord Rudra, and Paśupati; || 10.1064 ||
Īśāna, Bhīma, Mahādeva, and Ugrasena—through these forms, Śarva brings about the creation of the world. (10.1065)
Earth, water, fire, air, ether, and the sun, as well as the sacrificer and the moon—these eight are known as this creation. (10.1066)
But while they abide there with their entire being, here they are established with only a single portion;
thus, O Goddess, it is situated above the world of Brahmā.
And upon the summit of Meru resides Īśāna; he is further described as having eight yogas, known by the name Śrīkaṇṭha, and likewise having his abode on Kailāsa.
The universe is pervaded and presided over by you through your eight forms beginning with Śarva;
those who here practice the saguṇa yoga of Maheśvara [attain this].
Through devotion, celibacy, truthfulness, and self-restraint, you have seen the Lord; there the wise go.
But having always beheld his mandala with supreme devotion, those seekers who have transcended duality enter there just as they are. || 10-1071 ||
Īśāna, then Umā’s husband, Ajeśa, and Ananta as well. || 10.1073 ||
And thus, there is one Śiva, and those twelve Śivas are remembered as all resembling saffron in hue and possessing a splendor equal to ten million suns.
Established within the various worlds of diverse forms and shapes,
above that is Vīrabhadra, the Lord and sovereign of the maṇḍala.
By attaining union with that, one does not indeed rejoice together [with it].
Beyond this, O Great Goddess, are the eight auspicious Mahādevas. (10.1076)
Mahādeva, Mahātejas, Vāmadeva, Bhavodbhava,
Ekapiṅgekṣaṇa, Īśāna, and likewise the supreme Bhuvaneśa.
The eight Mahādevas, together with Aṅguṣṭhamātra, are auspicious Śivas;
they are liberated from the collyrium of Māyā and are esteemed by the Supreme Lord.
The worlds within the principle of intellect have been described by me in brief;
above this, however, is the principle of the qualities (guṇa-tattva), which is established therein.
The three divine lines of gurus stand separated by their qualities; the first line is situated above Tamas. (10.1080)
Their names are stated correctly and in proper sequence:
Śiva, Prabhū, Vāmadeva, Varṇa, and Pratāpana.
Prahlāda, Uttama, Bhīma, Karāla, Piṅgala, Mahendra, Dinakṛt, Pratoda, and Dakṣa. || 10.1082 ||
Kalevara, Vikhyāta, and likewise Kaṭaṅkaṭa; Ambuhartṛ, Nārīśa, Śveta, and indeed the Ṛgveda. || 10.1083 ||
The Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, the very auspicious Atharvaveda,
Virūpākṣa, Jyeṣṭha, Vipra, and likewise Nārāyaṇa.
Kuṇḍodara, Yamapāla, Grahaṇeśa, and Pīḍana—
these are declared to be the first row, remembered as consisting of thirty-two Rudras.
And above the Rajas [world], the second row is described:
Śukla, Dāma, Sudāma, Lokākṣa, and Sūtra. (10.1086)
Suhotra, Ekapāda, Gṛdhra, Śikheśvara,
Gautama, Yogeśa, and likewise the other, Dadhivāhu.
And likewise Ṛṣabha, Gokarṇa, Deva, Guheśvara,
Guheśāna, Śikhaṇḍin, Jaṭī, Mālī, and Ugrata.
Bhṛgu, Śikhin, Śūlin, Sugati, Supālaka,
Aṭṭahāsa, Dāruka, and Lāṅgalin are the Tridaṇḍins.
Bhāvana and likewise Bhāvya, as well as the supreme Lakulīśa—these thirty Rudras are declared for the second row, O lady of excellent vows. (10.1090)
The third row, situated above Satva, is said to consist of Vedadhara, Dīrghabāhu, Ratibhūti, and Sthāṇuka. || 10-1091 ||
Sadyojāta, as well as Jhaṇṭī, Ṣaṇmukha, Caturānana, Cakrapāṇi, Kūrmākṣa, and Arddhanārīśa. || 10-1092 ||
And Samvartaka, Bhasmiśa, and Kāmanāśana;
likewise Kapālī, Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, and Vaṣaṭkāra. || 10.1093 ||
Vauṣaṭkāra, as well as Svāhā and Svadhā, are proclaimed;
this third row consists of twenty-one Rudras. (10.1094)
Endowed with the power of the yoga of knowledge, these supreme teachers sport,
liberated from the snares of saṃsāra and devoid of great delusion.
All the gurus have three eyes and possess the luster of pure crystal;
they are all omniscient, all-pervading, and bestowers of grace upon all.
The divine worlds of all are shaped like elephants; now learn from me who those Rudras are, starting from the intellect (buddhi) down to primordial nature (prakṛti). || 10-1097 ||
I shall now describe that which begins with Devayopaṣṭaka and ends with Garbha;
it is renowned as consisting of two hundred [yojanas] and is joined by eight worlds.
Likewise, O fair-faced one, others are included therein;
however, that which was spoken of as being above the qualities (guṇas) is proclaimed to be Pradhāna.
I shall describe briefly those Rudras who are established there:
Krodheśvara, Saṃvarta, Jyotis, Piṅgala, and Krūrakṛt.
Pañcāntaka, Ekavīra, Śikheda, Daśahita, and Īśvara—these Rudras are proclaimed as possessing great heroism within the realm of primordial nature (prakṛti). (10.1101)
That which is the ultimate limit of the qualities (guṇas) is here called Pradhāna.
Therefore, understand from me now the worlds within the principle of Puruṣa.
Ambhā, Salilatudyā, Dhṛti, Tuṣṭi, as well as Supārā, Sunetrā, and Sumārī; beyond these [are the others]. (10.1103)
Uttamāmbhasikā—these nine are proclaimed as the Tuṣṭas (the Contented):
Tārā, Sutārā, Tārayantī, and Pramodikā; || 10-1104 ||
Pramuditā, Modamānā, and likewise the other, Ramyakā,
as well as Sadāpramuditā— this is declared to be the group of eight Siddhis.
Aṇimā, laghimā, mahimā, and prāpti are proclaimed; likewise prākāmya, īśitva, and that which is called vasitva. || 10-1106 ||
Wherein the mastery over the power of desire and the eightfold [siddhis] beginning with atomization (aṇimā) are traditionally taught;
beyond this, listen now to the three rows of teachers and disciples.
Maskarī, Pūraṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Kapila, and Kāśa; as well as Sanatkumāra, Gautama, Vasiṣṭha, and Prāṃśuka. || 10-1108 ||
Kāśyapa, Anāśaketu, Gālava, Bhautika, Śākalpa, and the supreme sage Durvāsas were likewise proclaimed. || 10-1109 ||
And Vālmīki, O best of the Kurus, Parāśara with Gālava, Pippalāda, Saṃvarta, Vāyu, Puṣṭa, and Atidantika; || 10-1110 ||
Those beginning with Maskarī and ending with Bhadanta were proponents of both the seen and the unseen;
likewise were Jahnu, Tṛṇabindu, Muni, and Tārikṣa.
Vanāśraya, Dīrgha, Hotṛ, Jāgara, Agasti, Vasu, and Nāga are proclaimed as the preceptors (upādhyāyas). || 10-1112 ||
Śukra, Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Roma, Jamadagni-suta Urdhvabāhu, Sthūlaśiras, Bālakhilya, and Manuja are thus proclaimed. || 10.1113 ||
Vajra, Treya, Viśuddha, Śiva, Sucāru, Antaka, and Jahnādicāru—these are said to be the second row. (10.1114)
Harajhaṇṭī, Pradāru, and likewise Amareśa;
Kṛṣṇapiṅgeśarudra, Indrajit, Ṛṣabha, and Śiva. || 10-1115 ||
Yama and the renowned Krūra, Gaṅgādhara and Umāpati,
Bhūteśvara and Kapālī, and likewise Śaṅkara.
And they know him as Ardhanārīśvara and Piṅgala;
likewise Mahākāla, Saṃvarta, Maṇḍalī, and Ekavīraka.
Likewise, there is another renowned and excellent lord, Bhārabhūteśvara;
and there are twenty-five sages beginning with Jahnu and ending with Cāru. (10–1118)
The gurus beginning with Hara and ending with Dhruva are recorded as twenty;
these are declared to be the three rows of sages for both the teacher and the disciple.
O Goddess, I shall describe the eightfold knowledge of the channels in brief:
Iḍā, Indriṇī, Gaurī, Śānti, and likewise Śāntikarī; || 10-1120 ||
Mālā, Maulinī, Svāhā, and likewise Svadhā—these should be understood with effort; therefore, O lady of excellent vows, I shall speak further.
O lady of beautiful hips, I shall explain the eightfold division in brief and not at length:
the effect and the instrument, as well as pleasure, pain, and that which is beyond. (10.1122)
Knowledge and faith are to be understood as the means and likewise the cause;
the bonds of the body have been explained, and I shall now describe the tenfold dharma, O beloved.
Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, and freedom from greed; absence of anger, service to the guru, purity, contentment, and straightforwardness. || 10-1124 ||
This is the tenfold dharma by which one who performs dharma is so called;
now I shall explain to you how the sixteen transformations are to be purified.
Smell, taste, form, touch, and likewise sound—these are known as the five subtle elements (*tanmātra*). Now learn from me concerning the sense organs.
Speech, hands, feet, the anus, and the generative organ are known as the organs of action;
the ear, skin, eyes, tongue, and the nose is considered the fifth [organ of perception]. (10.1127)

O Goddess of the gods, the organs of perception are known to have the mind as their sixteenth; these are declared to be the snares of dharma, and the wise know them to be the qualities of the intellect.
Dharma, knowledge, detachment, and likewise supreme sovereignty; as well as non-dharma, ignorance, lack of detachment, and lack of power. (10.1129)
And I shall now declare, in due order, the threefold ego (ahaṅkāra):
that which is called the transformative (vaikārika), the passionate (tejasa), and the elemental (bhūtādi). || 10-1130 ||
Understand from me how purification occurs at the time of initiation:
one should purify the qualities of tamas, rajas, and sattva in their proper sequence.
Sound, touch, as well as form, taste, and smell as the fifth—
these are declared to be the sense objects, which must be purified with diligent effort.
Desire, anger, greed, delusion, and indeed malice; birth, death, old age, disease, hunger, thirst, and craving. || 10-1133 ||
Despondency, fear, or even great joy, as well as passion, emaciation, anxiety, miserliness, falsehood, and malice. (10–1134)
Illusion, envy, dharma, and adharma, as well as lack of self-mastery—know that these are adventitious; hear from me concerning the fetters of the groups.
The Goddess, Nandin, Mahākāla, Gaṇeśa, as well as Vṛṣabha, Bhṛṅgin, Caṇḍeśvara, and Kārttikeya is remembered as the eighth. || 10-1136 ||
Ananta, Sastanu, Sūkṣma, Śrīkaṇṭha, Śivottama, Śikhaṇḍin, Ekanetra, and likewise the supreme Ekarudra. (10–1137)
At the time of initiation, one should purify the fetters whose nature consists of the Lords of Knowledge (vidyeśvara);
these include those already mentioned as well as any others characterized by the descriptions given in other tantras.
Those [karmas] are to be purified through human effort; thereafter, the individual is liberated.
Beyond this, destiny (niyati) is to be known; regarding that, learn of the Rudras. || 10-1139 ||
Vāmadeva and Śarva, as well as Bhavodbhava;
Kaca, Deha, Prabhu, Dhātṛ, Cakra, and Avikrama. || 10-1140 ||
And the tenth is Suprabheda; in Niyati, Saṅkara is recorded.
That lotus which is situated in the heart—the Self is established therein. (10–1141)
Niyati is the petals, Ahaṃkāra the filaments, and Buddhi the pericarp;
Śivā is to be known as residing in the principle of Time (Kālatattva). I shall explain this in brief.
He is pure, awakened, fully enlightened, and profoundly tranquil; he is the supreme imperishable, Śiva, and indeed Aśiva, the auspicious, imperishable Lord Śambhu.
The ten Śivas should be known as residing in the principle of Time (kāla-tattva);
the Śaṅkaras are said to have a golden luster, while the Śivas resemble crystal.
O illustrious one, for each of them, a retinue has been specified:
one hundred million and sixteen thousand have been designated.
The worlds of all [beings] are said to be shaped like tortoises.
Above this are Hari and Hara; now learn from me regarding the principle of passion (rāgatatva).
Sudṛṣṭa, Supradṛṣṭa, Svarūpa, Rūpavardhana, Manonmana, and Mahāvīra are proclaimed as the Lords of Heroes (Vīreśas). || 10-1147 ||
I shall now declare those Rudras who are established within the principle of Vidyā:
Kalyāṇa, Piṅgala, Vabhru, Vīra, and likewise Prabhava.
Medhā, Tithicchedaka, and Dāhaka of the author of the scripture—these five disciples are likewise to be appointed; thus, these ten are proclaimed.
Now listen to those who reside in that world above the Kalita level:
Vāma, Jyeṣṭha, Rudra, Kāla, and Kalivikaraṇa. || 10.1150 ||
Balavikaraṇa, Balapramathana, Sarvabhūtadamana, and likewise Manonmana.
And I shall tell you by name the three Great Deities who are above:
Mahādeva, Mahātejas, and the majestic Mahājyotis.
The principle of Kalā has been fully explained to you in brief, O lady of virtuous vows.
These Rudras, O Great Goddess, are three-eyed and have the moon as their crest-jewel.
Surrounded on all sides by thousands of crores of Rudras,
they resemble pure crystal and are endowed with the power of yogic sovereignty.
Those spoken of by Rāga should be known as those who are preeminent in the power of knowledge and yoga;
they are indeed the authors of the Sūtras, whose worlds consist of the essence of jewels.
I shall explain briefly this illusion that exists above; having pervaded millions [of worlds], it is established throughout that entire extent. || 10-1156 ||
In that [realm], there are twelve highly fortunate Rudras of great power:
Gahana, Asādhya, and likewise the lord Harihara.
Daśeśāna, Deveśa, Tṛkaloka, and likewise Gopati are to be known as being in the lower casket within the principle of Māyā, O fair-faced one.
Kṣemīśa, Brahmaṇasvāmī, and likewise Vidyeśāna;
Viśveśa, Śiva, and Ananta is said to be the sixth.
These Rudras are proclaimed to reside in the upper [region] of the Āyāpuṭa;
in their midst is the Blessed One Ananteśa, the Lord of the World.
Having brought about their manifestation, the Lord acts according to his own will;
he is omniscient and the creator of all, intent upon both restraint and grace.
By the first division, however, twelve Rudras are proclaimed;
in this Tantra, it is explained how the Rudras are established within the principle of Māyā.
In that same way, O lady of excellent vows, I shall describe the second division;
and likewise, O Goddess, Gopati is situated below the knot.
Above the knots resides the universe; [the lords are] Tṛkala, Kṣemī, Śaiva, Brahmaṇādhipati, and Śiva as the fifth.
Above this, O Goddess, the infinite fetters (pāśas) are established;
they have indeed been described previously, and beyond that lies the family of the sages (ṛṣikulam).
The womb is indeed Vāgīśvarī, where one who is born is not born again;
Oṃkāra is Sādhya, and Dhātṛ is Daneśvara.
They say that meditation (dhyāna) is like ashes; the authoritative measures are both above and below. Then follow the five objects, the secret of Śiva, and the Rudrāṅkuśa.
The Heart, the Lalanā, the Vyūha, the Ādarśaka, and likewise the Ākarṣa; thus is the eighth proclaimed here.
O Goddess, surrounded by these many millions of Rudras,
they are variegated with various colors and adorned with diverse ornaments.
Accompanied by various women, they sport according to the will of their lord;
all are three-eyed, bearers of tridents, with matted hair, crescent moons, and crowns.
Possessing unimpaired power and majesty, they are the presiding lords of the principle of Māyā,
established within various worlds arranged in the form of circles.
Beyond this is Mahāmāyā, who deludes all living beings;
by her, who is an adversary without enmity, their intellects are led astray.
"Disputants here contend, 'This is reality, this is not';
but by abandoning right understanding, they certainly lead one onto a wrong path. (10.1173)
Those lowest of men who, through devotion to the Guru, God, Fire, and the Śāstra, are ignorant of the investigation into the liberation from the unreal and rely upon dry logic. || 10-1174 ||
Those who desire to find dharma in what is not dharma are merely being deluded by illusion; once severed by the sword of Śiva-initiation, that illusion shall never sprout again.
Above her is Mahāvidyā, the source of all sciences,
the imperishable treasury of the power of the creation and dissolution of the universe.
She alone, O Goddess, is proclaimed as the supreme Vāgeśī;
she is indeed recited as the Vidyā divided into eight groups.
I shall now declare those worlds in their proper order and according to the truth:
Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhī, Raudrī, Kālī, and Kalavikaraṇī.
And likewise Valavikaraṇī, as well as Balapramathanī, Damanī of all beings, and also Manonmanī. || 10-1179 ||
And there, from that [source], the nine Śaktis of the worlds arise;
they have the appearance of molten gold, possess five faces, and have three eyes.
Possessing unfailing vigor, they are omniscient, abiding everywhere and at all times;
approved by everyone, they are all adorned with every ornament. || 10-1181 ||
Complete with all the marks and endowed with all sovereign powers,
seventy-five million principal [deities] are established here.
